title: The Art of Awareness
description: Stories from Zen and the Sufis about the simplest and the most difficult thing of all: to be awake. A man who walks through his life asleep, the master who wrote one word, the musk deer, and Mulla Nasruddin searching for his key under the lamp. Then a guided meditation to close, so you can taste it yourself.

beats.say: My friend, you have woken up every morning of your life. You opened your eyes, you got up, you went to work. And yet... have you ever really been awake?
Not awake like the eyes. Awake like a lamp that is lit inside the house. Most of us live in a dark house... and we call it living.
Tonight I will tell you a few stories. Old ones, from Zen, and from the Sufis. And at the end we will sit together, close our eyes, and do nothing at all.
So don't try to understand. Understanding is the work of the mind. Just listen... the way you listen to the rain on the roof.
Watch a man in the morning. The alarm rings, he gets up, he shaves, he drinks his tea, he reads the newspaper. Not once is he there. It all happens by itself.
He walks to the railway station. He has walked this road ten thousand times. His feet know the way. And he himself is somewhere else... in yesterday's quarrel, in tomorrow's worry.
In the train he sits with a hundred other people, and each one is sleeping with open eyes. Each one is talking to himself, inside, without a pause.
At the office he types letters, signs papers, smiles at the boss. In the evening he comes home, and he cannot remember one single moment of the day.
This is how a whole life passes. Seventy years, eighty years... and the man was never at home. Somebody else was living in his house.
Don't laugh at him. Just look a little closer... and you will find his face in your own mirror.
There is a story from Japan. A man came to a Zen master and said: Please, write down for me the highest wisdom. Something I can hang on my wall.
The master took up his brush, and he wrote one word. Attention.
The man was disappointed. Is that all? he asked. Please, write something more. So the master wrote again. Attention. Attention.
Now the man was almost angry. But what does it mean, this attention? And the master said, very quietly: Attention means attention.
You see, he is not being clever. There is nothing to explain. You cannot explain light to someone who keeps his eyes closed. You can only say... open them.
All the methods, all the old books of the East, finally say only this one word. Attention. Be here. Be present in whatever you are doing.
Now let me give you a simple way in. Sit by the side of a busy road. Buses, bullock carts, bicycles, people shouting... and you are just sitting there.
You don't stop the traffic. You don't run after the buses. You don't fight with the bullock carts. You simply watch them come... and go.
The mind is exactly like this road. A thought comes, a memory comes, a desire, a fear. And you are standing in the middle of the road... fighting all of them.
Step out of the road. Sit on the side. Let the thoughts pass. Don't call them good, don't call them bad. Just watch.
And slowly, slowly, you will notice something strange. The traffic becomes less. There are gaps. One thought has gone, and the next one has not yet come.
In that gap... you are. Not your name, not your work, not your worries. Only a pure silence, watching. That gap is the door.
In the forests of the Himalaya there lives a small deer. And one day the deer smells a beautiful fragrance. Musk. The most wonderful smell in the whole world.
The deer goes mad with it. Where is it coming from? It runs through the forest, over the rocks, across the rivers... searching, searching.
Day and night it runs. It cannot eat, it cannot sleep. The fragrance is always there, just ahead of it, calling... and it is never found.
And the poor deer does not know that the musk is inside its own body. It is carrying the very thing it is searching for.
We are all musk deer. Searching for joy in money, in fame, in another person... running from one marketplace to the next.
The fragrance you are looking for is not out there. It never was. Stop running, just for one moment... and smell it. It is you.
Let us try it with something difficult. Anger. Somebody insults you in the marketplace, and the fire rises, from the belly to the head.
Ordinarily you have two choices. Either you throw it out... you shout, you fight. Or you swallow it, you smile, and it burns inside you for years.
There is a third way, and it is very simple. Watch it. Close your eyes, and look at the anger the way a scientist looks through his microscope.
Don't judge it. Don't push it away. Just see it. Where is it in the body? How hot is it? How does it move?
And you will be surprised. The moment you watch it, the anger begins to cool. It cannot live in the light of awareness. It needs your sleep to survive.
The anger comes, and the anger goes. And you remain... untouched, like the sky after the storm.
Mulla Nasruddin was crawling on his knees under the street lamp one night. A neighbour came along and asked: Mulla, what have you lost?
My key, said Nasruddin. So the neighbour got down on his knees too, and they both searched, and searched, for a long, long time.
At last the neighbour said: Mulla, are you sure you lost it here? No, no, said Nasruddin. I lost it inside my house.
Then why on earth are we looking out here? And Nasruddin said: Because there is more light here, of course!
We all laugh. But this is exactly what every one of us is doing. The key is lost inside... and we search outside, because outside there is light, and people, and noise.
Inside it is dark. It is unfamiliar. But the key is there, and only there. Take the lamp of awareness... and turn it around.
The old Zen people had a saying. Before enlightenment, chop wood, carry water. After enlightenment... chop wood, carry water.
Nothing changes on the outside. The same wood, the same well, the same work. But the one who is doing it has changed completely.
So you don't need to run away to the Himalaya. Your kitchen is enough. Your office is enough. Washing the dishes is enough.
When you eat, just eat. Taste the rice. When you walk, just walk. Feel the earth under your feet. And when you drink your tea... only drink.
This is all that meditation is. Not some strange ritual. Just doing whatever you are doing... with your whole presence.
Then every moment becomes a small temple. And the whole day becomes a prayer without words.
Now... let us sit together. Find a comfortable place. Let your back be straight, but not stiff. And close your eyes.
Take one deep breath... and let it go. Another one... and let it go. Now don't control the breath. Let it come and go by itself.
Just watch the breath. It comes in... it goes out. Coming in... going out. You are only a watcher, sitting on the bank of the river.
Thoughts will come. Let them come. Don't fight. See them the way you see clouds passing in the sky... and come back to the breath.
Sounds from the street, a dog barking far away, a scooter passing. Let them all be there. You are not disturbed by them. You are only watching.
Now go a little deeper. Watch the one who is watching. Who is this, sitting here, aware? Don't answer. Just look.
Silence... only silence. Rest in it. Nothing to do. Nowhere to go. Nobody to be.
And slowly, slowly... take one deep breath. Bring this silence with you. When you are ready, open your eyes. Thank you, my friend.
